findings.reason: the node's gate would close on half the deliverable, and the 90.9-minute wait the Why records is the wait for the review dispatch as much as for promotion, so a node that skips it leaves the larger share of the measured delay in place.
findings.text: §70's done-when reads only that a run "whose review comes back clean" ends "promoted and landed with no coordinator call", so the deliverable's first clause, that "a delivered run's review is dispatched without a coordinator", has no measure; a test that plants a review verdict and drives promotion alone passes the gate while review dispatch stays manual

findings.reason: as written two runs writing one crew-home file are both admitted, and the fix would have to narrow the rule to unowned shared paths (or keep the exclusive-write escape the repository case preserves) rather than exempting the whole directory.
findings.text: §69's deliverable exempts "a path in the shared crew home" without distinguishing a shared directory from a path one run owns there, while the Why's evidence is a "path every run touches and no run owns"; the second test controls only a claim "inside the repository", so a claim on a crew-home path a run does own is exempted by the rule and covered by no test

findings.reason: the later window cannot distinguish a lane whose crew-home holds were fixed from one whose holds merely moved to another root, so §67 could close on a record that does not measure the defect it credits §69 with removing.
findings.text: §69's Why asserts "5 of 8 admission passes held a request on a claim under the shared crew home", but §9's declared record (plan.html:96) reports only "the number of admit passes holding a request on a claim", with no total pass count and no claim root, so neither the 5-of-8 figure nor §67's later target of "no admission pass holding a request on a claim under a shared root" (plan.html:342) can be read from the record it cites
